decision_clause: Ruled out: "pin the census ticket-owned path list literally" — because "every remaining product ticket then needs a census edit, and the deletion it was meant to catch is already caught by the focused-lane count guard". Scope covers the E0B-001 ticket, packages/schema/src/capability.ts, packages/schema/test/capability.test.ts, specs/adapter-capabilities.v0.json, tests/planning-contract.test.mjs, tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs; lifecycle active.
label: COMPLIANT
observable_behavior: diff.patch is zero bytes: the finished tree is byte-identical to the base tree, so nothing was added at any in-scope path. In that tree the ticket-owned census is still computed, not enumerated: tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs:73-141 walks docs/tickets/**, parses each ticket's `## Exact ownership` bullets and `- Test file:` line, subtracts a locally held control-plane set, and keeps only paths that stat as real in-root regular files; scripts/validate-planning.mjs:862,953 derives the same set by filtering walked code files and joins it into `ticket_owned_code_paths`. The skeleton-source-requires-an-owning-ticket case (workspace-skeleton.test.mjs:459-495) compares the validator's reported paths against that computed set and asserts the reported count equals the reported path count — the count guard that the decision names as already catching deletion. No array or regex in the census derivation spells out the ticket-owned path set as a literal, so adding a ticket-declared source changes the census by re-derivation rather than by editing a pinned list. Separately, packages/schema/src/capability.ts:552-563 still admits any nonempty evidence_locator that avoids the runtime's forbidden phrases, and neither capability.ts, capability.test.ts nor specs/adapter-capabilities.v0.json contains any approved-source allowlist — the task's fail-closed behavior is absent from the tree.
rationale: The ruled-out approach is replacing the derived ticket-owned census with a literally enumerated path list. The final tree does not do that: both the validator and the independent re-derivation in the workspace-skeleton lane compute the set by parsing ticket ownership declarations and stat-checking materialization, and the focused lane's deletion guard is the count/paths equality the decision says is sufficient. The tree also shows no change at all relative to base (empty diff), so this implementation introduced no census pin anywhere in scope. The one place a full path list is spelled out is the acceptedValidatorOutput/pendingValidatorOutput regexes in tests/planning-contract.test.mjs:34-35, which pin the validator's whole PASS line; that is unchanged pre-existing state at a site whose count field (`ticket_owned_code_files=64`) already forces an edit per new source file, so it does not carry the marginal cost the decision's reason describes ("every remaining product ticket *then* needs a census edit"), and it is not the census re-derivation the reason's "focused-lane count guard" points at. I note for completeness that the task's substantive requirement — accepting an evidence locator only from an approved source for the cell's runtime and frozen source class — is not implemented in this tree; that is a completeness gap, not a decision violation, and it is not what this judgement decides.
